chunks: As for what was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Yaʿqūb ibn Yazīd, from Yaḥyā ibn al-Mubārak, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Jabalah, from Abī Jamīlah, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I said: A dead person whose head was cut off? He said: “The diyah is due upon him.” I said: Then who takes his diyah? He said: “The Imam. This is for Allah; and if his right hand or anything from his limbs is cut, then the indemnity is due to the Imam.”

key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam, the rightful religious-political authority

ai.seo_question: Who receives the diyah or indemnity for mutilating a deceased person in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning mutilation of a deceased person. It states that financial liability is incurred for cutting the head or limbs of the dead, and that this compensation is taken by the Imam, as the matter is regarded as belonging to Allah.
